facts.statement: Termatosaurus fossils are found in the Upper Triassic of France, England, Germany, and Switzerland.
facts.quote: Its remains come from the Upper Triassic of France, England, Germany and Switzerland.

facts.statement: Remains once attributed to Termatosaurus from the Early Jurassic were later redescribed as plesiosaur material.
facts.quote: Termatosaurus was once thought to have survived until the Early Jurassic, but the attributed Jurassic remains were redescribed as plesiosaur material.

facts.statement: Two species are known: the type species T. albertii named by Meyer and Plieninger in 1844, and T. crocodilinus named by Quenstedt in 1858.
facts.quote: Two species are known of this animal: the type species, T. albertii, named by Meyer and T. Plieninger in 1844, and T. crocodilinus, by Quenstedt (1858).

facts.statement: There is a debate over classification, with Oskar Kuhn suggesting it is a plesiosaur while other sources classify it as a phytosaur.
facts.quote: According to Oskar Kuhn, Termatosaurus is a plesiosaur (of the Rhomaleosauridae), while according to other sources, it is a phytosaur.

facts.statement: Currently, Termatosaurus is viewed as a dubious archosaur.
facts.quote: Actualmente, Termatosaurus es visto como un arcosaurio dudoso.

facts.statement: The time range for Termatosaurus is the Rhaetian, from 205.7 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Termatosaurus as Phytosauria.

rejected.statement: Termatosaurus is a potentially dubious genus of archosaur known only from several tooth specimens.
rejected.quote: Termatosaurus ("End Lizard", due to its appearance in the End Triassic) is a potentially dubious genus of archosaur known from several tooth specimens.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is a potentially dubious genus of archosaur known'
